title: Saturn Grew a 10-Sided Polar Pattern
hook: Saturn's north pole has worn a giant hexagon for decades. Hubble now shows the south pole sprouting its own polygon — this one with ten sides, and still sharpening.
key_points: A huge 10-sided atmospheric pattern has appeared around Saturn's south pole.
It mirrors, but doesn't match, the long-known six-sided jet stream at the north pole.
Hubble data suggest the decagon only emerged within the past few years.
The pattern is still growing stronger, so it wasn't a one-off fluke of the weather.
Why polar jets lock into straight-edged polygons at all remains unexplained.
content_html: Saturn's north pole has been circled by an enormous six-sided jet stream since Voyager first glimpsed it — one of the strangest weather features in the solar system. Now, according to a ScienceDaily report, NASA scientists using Hubble have found the planet's south pole growing a polygon of its own: a giant pattern with ten sides.
extra_html: The decagon appears to be new. Hubble's record suggests it only started emerging in the past few years, and it is still sharpening rather than fading, which argues against a passing quirk of the weather. That leaves the interesting questions wide open: why a swirling polar jet should lock into straight edges and corners at all, why the south chose ten sides where the north settled on six, and whether this one will persist for decades like its northern cousin. Continued observations are the plan.

related.title: Solving Saturn's Spin Mystery
related.hook: Saturn's measured spin rate kept drifting, baffling astronomers for decades. The James Webb telescope reveals the planet wasn't speeding up — its winds were fooling us.

related.title: Why Some Giant Planets Spin Faster Than 'Failed Stars'
related.hook: Astronomers clocked the spins of dozens of distant worlds and found a surprise: lightweight giant planets can twirl faster than the much heavier brown dwarfs — so mass isn't the whole story.

flashcards.prompt: What did Hubble spot around Saturn's south pole?
flashcards.back_html: A giant 10-sided (decagon) atmospheric pattern — a southern counterpart to the famous six-sided pattern that rings Saturn's north pole.

flashcards.prompt: Why do researchers think the south-polar decagon is a recent development?

choices.text: Hubble data show it only began emerging in the past few years, and it is still strengthening
It was photographed by Voyager in the 1980s and has since faded
It appears and vanishes with every Saturnian day

flashcards.explanation_html: The Hubble record indicates the pattern started showing up only within the last few years and continues to grow stronger, rather than being a long-standing or fleeting feature.

flashcards.prompt: What makes Saturn's polar polygons scientifically puzzling?
flashcards.back_html: A jet stream is a smooth, curving band of wind — yet at Saturn's poles it settles into shapes with straight edges and sharp corners, and nobody knows why one suddenly formed in the south or how long it will last.
